profile.essay_draft:
The robot moved twelve centimeters and stopped. I had spent three evenings
adjusting the wheels, and I was certain the motor was the problem. A younger
teammate asked whether we had checked the battery connection. We had not.

I was captain of our first prototype team. That title made it tempting to answer
every question before someone else could. After the battery incident, I began
asking each teammate to propose a test before we changed a part. Our notebook
filled with failed hypotheses, but our decisions became easier to explain.

Tutoring changed my understanding of that process. When a student asked why a
fraction became larger after division, repeating the rule did not help. Drawing
an example did. I began bringing sketches to robotics meetings, too. I want to
study mechanical engineering because I enjoy translating a confusing problem
into something a team can inspect, test, and improve together.
